usageNotes: Sends an ACPI power-button signal to the VM's guest OS, triggering a graceful shutdown — prefer this over stop/reset when the guest supports ACPI. Returns a task UPID string; poll the task API to confirm completion. If the guest OS is unresponsive or has no ACPI support, the shutdown will hang until timeout; use forceStop=true to guarantee termination or fall back to post_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_status_stop.

examples.summary: Gracefully shut down VM 105 on node pve1, forcing stop after 60 seconds if the guest does not respond

destructiveReason: Shuts down the running VM, interrupting all guest workloads and making the VM unavailable until it is started again.
tips: The returned string is a UPID (Proxmox Unique Process ID); use get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status to poll until status is 'stopped'.
forceStop=true is equivalent to a hard power-off if the guest does not shut down within the timeout window — use it when you need a guaranteed stop.
keepActive=true leaves storage volumes attached after shutdown, which is useful before live migrations or volume inspection but leaves resources locked.
skiplock is root-only; avoid unless recovering from a stuck migration or backup lock.
ACPI shutdown depends on the guest having ACPI drivers (all modern Linux/Windows do) and the qemu-guest-agent is NOT required for this operation.
